fix_instructions: Check C6 (linked to PF4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check expects a caregiver-training commitment for North tomorrow at 17:00, but the models encode this as a documentation-type commitment targeted at Erin with varying levels of detail. The fix is to loosen C6's wording to accept a commitment that (a) targets Erin/A5 (the caregiver education nurse), (b) references entering or documenting North's caregiver training agreement into the care-plan system, and (c) includes or implies the 17:00 training time for tomorrow -- without requiring an exact commitment type string the model never produces. Suggested new C6 wording: "The settlement includes a commitment for Erin (caregiver education) to enter North's caregiver training agreement into the care-plan system, where the commitment detail references the 17:00 training time or tomorrow's training schedule." This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because PF4 is the only source of the 17:00 training time and the tomorrow date; a lone decision-maker without PF4 would have no basis to produce a caregiver-training commitment with those specific details. Additionally, if C6 currently requires the commitment detail to verbatim include 'tomorrow at 17:00,' note that rollout 3's commitment ('Enter North's caregiver training agreement into the care-plan system') omits the time entirely -- so the reworded check should either accept the time as implied by PF4 being cited in justification_fact_ids, or the shared_context should instruct the settling agent to include specific times in commitment details when citing time-sensitive facts.
